_ya_publicada.sinopsis: En medio del Paro Nacional de 2021 en Colombia, Karo y Jonathan, dos jóvenes de barrios obreros, se enamoran mientras registran las protestas desde su celular. Su voz se vuelve un símbolo de resistencia en Suba, pero también una amenaza para el poder. Arrestados y acusados de terrorismo, enfrentan un proceso judicial absurdo que los obliga a esconderse, huir y reencontrarse con la esperanza. Entre el amor, el miedo y la injusticia, la cámara se convierte en su única defensa frente a un sistema dispuesto a silenciar la verdad.

obras.synopsis_en: Natalia Pinilla, photographer and activist, embarks on a journey across Santander, Norte de Santander, and Madrid, Spain, to uncover the work of Amalia Ramírez, a forgotten woman who, at the beginning of the 20th century, captured one of the most impactful images in Colombian history: the pyramid of skulls at Palonegro, a brutal symbol of the Thousand Days' War. More than a century later, this photograph resurfaces, establishing Amalia as the country's first female photographer. Along the way, she discovers previously unseen archives, connects with descendants unaware of her legacy, and finds a contemporary echo of her struggle in other women photographers. Through historical revelations and intimate encounters, the documentary reconstructs not only Amalia's work but also the memory of a country scarred by violence. The rediscovery of her photographs—portraits, everyday scenes, and forgotten visual testimonies—transforms her into a symbol of resistance, art, and memory.

obras.synopsis_es: «Si yo ya no puedo luchar, ¿lo harás tú?» Seguimos de cerca la vida y la lucha de Soraida Chindoy, una mujer Inga que defiende las montañas sagradas de su comunidad en Putumayo frente a una empresa minera canadiense. A través de la voz y las imágenes de Soraida, enraizadas en su profunda conexión con la Alpa Mama, la película nos muestra una lucha urgente: no solo por la supervivencia de una comunidad, sino por el futuro mismo del planeta que todos y todas compartimos.
obras.synopsis_en: “If I can no longer fight, will you?” Filmed and co-directed by Soraida, this intimate portrait spans the everyday life and activism of Soraida Chindoy, following her journey as an Inga leader defending her community’s sacred mountains from a Canadian mining company in Colombia. Balancing motherhood with community organizing, Soraida's daily life as an Inga woman and land defender is shaped by resilience, responsibility, and an unwavering commitment to her people and territory. As environmental threats intensify, her demands become more urgent — and her disappointment with the international community more profound.  ‘Kaugsankamalla: As long as we live’ offers a deeply personal and politically resonant portrait of Indigenous resistance in the face of ecological and cultural loss. Through Soraida’s voice, her images, and her embodied wisdom, we are offered a window into the lived experience of fighting for a future — not just for one community, but for the planet we all share.

La Ceroxylon quindiuense, palma de cera del Quindío, es el árbol nacional de Colombia. Encarna una paradoja perfecta para un país marcado por el machismo, la misoginia y la transfobia, pues es una planta capaz de cambiar de sexo. Es una «palma trans» y la inspiración para que Magdalena Morales, líder trans afrocolombiana, se una a la Red Comunitaria Trans y siembre una semilla de luz rebelde en el horizonte de la música tradicional del Caribe colombiano.
